interfaces.interface_notes: The FCC Cu-rich particles at the β-Mn interfaces contain frequently observed FCC twins (b0058); the amount of FCC Cu-rich phase between β-Mn interfaces decreases with increasing Al content, and the BCC phase forms at β-Mn interfaces due to Al enrichment (b0068).
interfaces.phase_evolution: α (BCC) matrix → α + FCC Cu-rich phase + α-Mn → β-Mn + BCC phase + FCC Cu-rich phase. At 625 °C (≥600 °C) the α→β-Mn transformation of the 17Al alloy was almost complete within 1 h of aging, with BCC and FCC Cu-rich phases forming at the β-Mn interfaces.

comparative_performance.comparison_metric: peak Vickers hardness and fracture toughness decrease with increasing Al content (17Al vs 15Al)

processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Alloy ingots with nominal composition Fe-35Mn-17Al-5Cu (at.%) produced by melting high-purity (>99.9%) raw materials in a vacuum induction furnace under an argon atmosphere.
The ingots were homogenized at 1200 °C for 24 h.
After homogenization the ingots were hot-rolled into plates with a thickness of 4 mm.
processing_steps.reduction_ratio: hot-rolled into plates with a thickness of 4 mm

processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Plates were cut into 10 × 5 × 2 mm³ samples using electrical discharge machining for Vickers hardness measurements and microstructure characterizations.
Samples were solution treated at 1100 °C for 10 min under an argon atmosphere, followed by oil quenching (parent process proc_st-1100c-10min-oq).
Solution-treated samples were aged at 625 °C for 6 h followed by water quenching; this defines the sample state (17Al aged at 625 °C for 6 h).

measurement_conditions.other_conditions: Vickers hardness measured with an HVS-1000 digital microhardness tester at a load of 9.8 N for 15 s; each sample tested 5 times and reported as the average of 5 measurements.

phases_present.morphology: dominant transformed phase (α matrix almost completely transformed into β-Mn)
fine particles distributed at the interfaces between β-Mn; FCC twins frequently observed within the particles

structures.overall_structure: After aging the 17Al Fe-35Mn-17Al-5Cu low-density steel at 625 °C for 6 h (a temperature ≥600 °C), the α (BCC) matrix had almost completely transformed into β-Mn, with numerous fine BCC and FCC precipitates distributed within the β-Mn. The β-Mn is a Mn-rich phase poor in Al and Cu.

unmapped_findings: The 17Al alloy's Vickers hardness across the 625 °C aging series (Table 3) is nearly time-independent: 813.0 ± 20.8 HV (1 h), 872.0 ± 24.4 HV (3 h), 878.4 ± 28.3 HV (6 h, this sample) and 870.5 ± 24.9 HV (10 h).
The parent solution-treated 17Al Fe-35Mn-17Al-5Cu alloy (proc_st-1100c-10min-oq baseline) has a Vickers hardness of 259.8 ± 1.5 HV (Table 3, merged cell).
The peak Vickers hardness of the 17Al alloy (924.9 HV) was reached at 575 °C for 6 h, not at 625 °C/6 h; this peak was lower than the 15Al peak (965.6 HV).
The fracture toughness K_IC of the hardest 17Al sample (575 °C/6 h, 924.9 HV) was 6.6 MPa·m^1/2, measured by the indentation technique using Eq. (1).
The 17Al alloy has a Young's modulus of 175 GPa (from compressive stress-strain curves), used in the indentation fracture-toughness calculation.
For the hardest 17Al sample, the intrinsic β-Mn hardness measured by nanoindentation was 12.2 ± 0.1 GPa and the average nanoindentation hardness was 11.1 ± 0.6 GPa.
SEM-EDS of β-Mn in the hardest 17Al sample gave Mn 36.2 at.%, Al 16.3 at.% and Cu 2.6 at.%.
The volume fraction of FCC Cu-rich and BCC precipitates at β-Mn interfaces for the 17Al alloy aged at 650 °C for 10 h was 4.7 % (Vickers hardness 833.2 HV).
